newsitem.title: CHINA: One HK player conspicuous by absence at handover.
newsitem.headline: One HK player conspicuous by absence at handover.

text.p: One of China's key players in the recovery of Hong Kong, the man who signed the treaty sealing the handover of the British colony, will not see the spectacular ceremonies. He will be under house arrest.

Zhao Ziyang was China's premier and sat beside British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher at a broad table in the Great Hall of the People on December 19,1984, to sign the Joint Declaration that ensured the handover of Hong Kong.

As premier, Zhao also oversaw the elaborate and complicated negotiations between Britain and China in the early 1980s that led up to that treaty under which 156 years of British colonial rule come to an end at midnight on Monday.
He signed the landmark treaty while his patron, the late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping whose "one country, two systems" formula ensured the handover, stood behind him smiling and applauding.

Zhao will be elsewhere when the other treaty signatory, Margaret Thatcher, attends the handover ceremony at midnight in Hong Kong along with Zhao's successor as Communist Party chief, Jiang Zemin, and Deng's widow Zhuo Lin.

China's former premier and party chief, once Deng's anointed heir, will almost certainly be watching the ceremony on television in his Beijing courtyard home where he has lived under virtual house arrest since his overthrow after the 1989 student-led pro-democracy demonstrations.
The protests were crushed by the army on June 4, 1989, with heavy loss of life.
Zhao was criticised for sympathising with the demonstrators and dismissed from all his party and government posts in June, 1989
He emerges occasionally from his Beijing home to play golf.
